correctness.rationale: Original RESULT.md line 87 overstates the deterministic minor identity: for A=[[0,1],[1,0]] the only selectable corners each leave a residual of norm 1, whereas the stated right side is 2. The repaired RESULT.md restricts the factor 4 to nonzero entries and gives the exact nonzero-corner count otherwise, by summing the squared pivot cancellation only over selectable pivots. Gaussian inputs have no zero entries almost surely, so this repair does not change the unconditional second moment or main theorem. Independently, for a fixed complement and t>||W|| the tail event is (t^2-||W||^2)x^2+2<W,uv^T>x-||u||^2||v||^2<0; its two roots multiplied by t tend to -h and h, h=||u||||v||. Integrating the x-squared selection weight gives 2 f(0)h^3/(3S). On ||W||≤t/2 the scaled integral is dominated by a constant times h^3/S≤S^2/8, and the Gaussian complement outside this event gives o(t^-3). The Gaussian chi-square Laplace integrals for E[(UV)^(3/2)/S] have total power (mn-1)/2+3, giving the displayed 8/(mn+3) times the gamma ratios. Layer cake and the radial Gaussian second-moment calculation verify the remaining assertions. These are analytic checks, not claims of a new Monte Carlo run.
residual_risks: One exact step, real matrices, fixed dimensions and common strictly positive Gaussian noise scale; no uniform small-noise, multistep, or finite-precision claim.
